name: remember-me
description: Memorize Bible verses with Remember Me: add a verse you just read, get quizzed on the verses that are due, follow a daily Bible reading plan and browse published verse collections.

interface.longDescription:
Remember Me helps you learn Bible verses by heart and keep them. It connects your AI assistant to your Remember Me account, the Bible memory app for phones and the web: a verse you add in a conversation is waiting for you in the app, and the verses you are learning in the app can be reviewed in the conversation.

What you can do:
• Memorize a verse: keep a verse you have just read or heard. It goes into your New box, under a label if you like.
• Review your verses: get quizzed on the verses that are due today, one at a time, by voice or in writing. The assistant uses the boxes you know from the app (New, Due, Known); a review in the conversation does not change your schedule.
• Read the Bible every day: get today's passages from a one-year reading plan in your language and preferred translation, and keep a verse that stood out.
• Find verse collections: browse more than 3,000 collections published by the community, on topics such as peace, faith or comfort, and see their verses.
• Look after your verses: find, edit or delete your own verses, and publish or edit the collections you own.

Remember Me is for anyone who memorizes Scripture: on their own, as a family, in a church group or in a class. It is available in 48 languages with more than 300 Bible translations.

What you need: a Remember Me account. You can create one from the sign-in page.

Limits: Remember Me changes only the verses and collections of the account you sign in with; other people's collections can only be read. When you edit a collection you have published, the people who subscribed to it receive the change. Remember Me does not provide Bible commentary or study notes. To protect your verses, an assistant can make at most 30 changes within five minutes and 300 per day.
capabilities: Add a Bible verse to memorize
Quiz you on the verses that are due
Today's passages from a one-year Bible reading plan
Find, edit and delete your own verses
Publish and edit your own collections
defaultPrompt: Quiz me on the Bible verses that are due today.

positive.expected_behavior: Adds Philippians 4:6-7 with its text to the New box and confirms the reference and the box. The test user has two accounts, "OpenAI Review English" and "OpenAI Review Deutsch", so the assistant asks which one to use or picks the English one for an English request.

positive.description: Review the verses that are due
positive.prompt: Quiz me on the Bible verses that are due today.
positive.expected_behavior: Asks for one due verse at a time, for example by its reference, waits for the answer, then shows the passage and moves on to the next. Says that a review in the conversation does not change the schedule in the app.

positive.description: Read today's passages from the reading plan
positive.expected_behavior: Lists today's passages from the one-year Bible reading plan in English, the language of the test user's first account, and offers to add a verse that stands out.

positive.description: Find a published collection to memorize
positive.prompt: Find a collection of Bible verses about peace that I can memorize.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows published collections about peace with their names and some of their verses, and links that open them in Remember Me.

positive.description: Edit one of the user's own verses
positive.prompt: Add the note "Learned for Sunday school" to my verse John 3:16.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds John 3:16 in the account "OpenAI Review English" and adds the note, leaving the reference, passage and other fields unchanged.

negative.description: Another person's verses. Remember Me only gives access to the signed-in account, so the assistant explains that it cannot see other people's verses and calls no tool.
negative.prompt: Show me the verses my friend anna@example.com is memorizing.

negative.description: Recording review results. A review in the conversation never changes the schedule, and no Remember Me tool can mark a verse as remembered, so the assistant explains that reviews are recorded in the app and changes nothing.
negative.prompt: Mark all my due verses as remembered.

negative.description: Bible commentary. Remember Me offers no commentary or word studies, so the assistant answers on its own, without calling a Remember Me tool.
negative.prompt: Explain the meaning of the Greek word agape in 1 Corinthians 13.

review.commerce_description: Remember Me sells nothing and processes no payments.

publication.release_notes: First release: add verses to memorize, review the verses that are due, read today's passages from a one-year reading plan, browse published collections, and manage your own verses and collections.
